title: Redwood + BlueCrest Health - Security & Privacy Review
summary: High-level security & privacy review focused on data handling: prompt retention, PII/PHI handling, encryption/KMS options, SOC 2 evidence, and contractual 'no training on customer data' assurances. Customer requires documentation for SOC2, encryption diagrams, and a written confirmation that Redwood does not use customer data to train models. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs; BlueCrest is leaning toward a private or dedicated deployment for PHI workloads but wants pilot with proof points.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Send SOC 2 Type II report and latest penetration test summary by 2025-12-15
Priya Singh: Prepare a KMS/CMK architecture diagram and notes on HSM integration by 2025-12-16
Priya Singh: Run a short pilot plan for dedicated capacity (30-day) and share ops checklist by 2025-12-19
Marta Ruiz: Provide redacted sample PHI prompt examples and compliance hits by 2025-12-18
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 + ISO materials and encryption architecture
Schedule follow-up technical deep dive with BlueCrest engineers (Priya SE + Liam) week of 12/22
Agree on pilot scope for dedicated/private environment and finalize data retention settings
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Lee (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our security SE. Quick roll call?
00:08 Marta Ruiz (CISO): Marta here, CISO at BlueCrest.
00:10 Ethan Cole (Head of IT): Ethan, IT lead.
00:12 Dr. Priya Nair (Compliance): Priya Nair, compliance.
00:15 Liam Park (Eng): Liam, engineering.
00:18 Priya Singh (SE): Hi all, thanks. We'll go through the security checklist you sent and call out anything special for PHI.
00:25 Jordan: Goal today is to confirm controls around prompt retention, PII/PHI handling, encryption, SSO/RBAC, and the contractual statement about training on customer data.
00:35 Marta: Great, we're sensitive to PHI so we have to be very sure about retention and who can see logs. Also SOC2 evidence for legal.
00:42 Priya: Absolutely. Quick high level: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private. For PHI most customers prefer dedicated or private - we can do VPC peering and customer-managed keys. For hosted, we have stricter safeguards but we don't recommend it for active PHI unless you have BAAs in place.
00:58 Marta: Can you confirm you do not use customer prompts or outputs to train models?
01:02 Priya: Yes, let me be explicit — Redwood does not use customer prompt or content to train our base models. We have a policy and contractual language we can provide. That's for the hosted API; if a customer opts in to data-sharing for model improvements that's a separate opt-in process and is spelled out in the contract.
01:20 Ethan: Where do the audit logs live and who has access? We need immutable logs for any access to PHI.
01:26 Priya: Audit logs are retained in our logging system by default for 90 days for hosted; for Dedicated/Private we can configure retention — customers often push logs into their own Splunk/Datadog via secure forwarder or S3 with lifecycle rules. Access controls: RBAC ties into SAML SSO and you can map roles to limit access to keys, logs, and consoles.
01:45 Liam: How granular is RBAC? Can we lock down token-level or per-route access?
01:49 Priya: You can create roles that scope to model endpoints, routes, and even token usage. For Dedicated/Private, you have full control and can disable certain admin capabilities. There are also audit trails for token issuance.
02:05 Marta: About encryption — we need AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit, and customer-managed keys with HSM backing. Is that supported?
02:13 Priya: Yes. We support AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2/1.3. For Hosted we offer KMS integration with major cloud providers; for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own CMK (customer-managed key) and integrate with an HSM or KMS. We'll provide an architecture diagram showing envelope encryption and key rotation.
02:32 Ethan: And data residency? BlueCrest must keep data in the US.
02:35 Priya: You can pin region. Our hosted API has region controls, Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in a specific region, and Private deploys in your VPC or on-prem. We'll map out region-specific options.
02:44 Marta: Retention policy specifics — do you retain prompts or logs by default, and can we configure immediate deletion?
02:50 Priya: Defaults: hosted retains logs for 90 days; prompt/content retention depends on the plan. We offer an option to disable content retention entirely for sensitive workloads and to delete KV cache/prefix caches after each session. For Dedicated/Private you have full control and can set TTLs or enable automatic purge on ingest. We'll document exact API calls to purge.
03:10 Dr. Priya Nair: About PHI — in addition to technical controls, we need contract language (BAA) and evidence that backups, snapshots, and any intermediate caches are not accessible to other customers.
03:22 Jordan: We can do BAAs for the right deployment types. For hosted we have an addendum in some regions; Dedicated/Private is the common path for PHI and we can include BAA. Backups for Dedicated are isolated; for Private it's customer-controlled.
03:34 Marta: How about redaction tooling — can Redwood do automated PII/PHI scrubbing before storage?
03:40 Priya: We have pre-processing hooks you can run to redact or tokenise PII before it reaches the runtime. Customers also run a preprocess lambda in their VPC.
03:48 Ethan: We need a written confirmation we mentioned earlier: a statement that data will not be used to train models. Can you put that in writing?
03:55 Jordan: Yes, we will provide a written confirmation — standard clause we include: "Redwood will not use Customer Data to train, improve, or update models without Customer's prior written consent." We'll attach the clause and the legal appendix.
04:08 Liam: What about ephemeral keys and session tokens — how are those rotated?
04:12 Priya: API tokens are issued; for short-lived sessions we recommend OAuth with SAML assertions. Keys can be rotated via KMS; we support automatic rotation windows and manual rotation.
04:24 Marta: Are there any known gaps or high-risk items we should be aware of?
04:27 Priya: For hosted, the main concerns are multi-tenant metadata (we can disable customer-tracking) and shorter log retention defaults. For Dedicated/Private, the risk surface is limited to your network and config; Redwood's runtime is hardened and we can run an architecture review. We'll document our SOC2 controls and pen test results.
04:45 Ethan: Can we get sample audit log entries to see format? Timestamp, user, action, resource, request id?
04:50 Priya: Yes — we'll send a sample log schema (JSON lines) and a sample event stream.
04:55 Marta: Also curious about detection and alerting — do you surface suspicious access attempts?
04:58 Priya: We have hooks into SIEM; we ship alerts for anomalous token usage, unusual geolocations, and privileged action spikes. Customers usually pipe those to their own PagerDuty/Splunk.
05:10 Jordan: Next, pricing/legal: some customers want encryption-at-rest with CMK in contract; we can include that as an add-on.
05:18 Dr. Priya Nair: Timeline — we need SOC2 evidence and the no-training confirmation by 12/18 to satisfy internal sign-off.
05:24 Jordan: Noted. We'll upload SOC2 and the legal clause by 12/15 and the encryption diagram by 12/16.
05:30 Marta: Pilot — we'd like to run a short dedicated pilot where we feed redacted PHI samples and run latency tests.
05:35 Priya: We'll scope a 30 day dedicated pilot, include ingress egress network diagrams, and optional workload-based quantization/latency testing.
05:44 Liam: On prompts: if a user types PHI into the chat, what happens to that content in the pipeline?
05:49 Priya: For Hosted default flow: content may transiently be processed and stored in logs for troubleshooting unless you enable content-retention disable or configure redaction hooks. For Dedicated/Private we can disable retention, and KV/prefix caches can be set to purge immediately. We'll outline API settings to enforce that.
06:05 Marta: Okay that's close to what we need. Anything else?
06:08 Ethan: A small nit — do you have SOC2 auditor contact or a report we can share with our auditors?
06:11 Jordan: Yes we'll provide the SOC2 Type II report and a point of contact for the auditor under NDA.
06:18 Priya: We'll also include the encryption key flow diagram and an example KMS policy JSON snippet.
06:22 Jordan: Recap: Redwood will: 1) deliver SOC2 + pen test summary by 12/15, 2) provide written no-training clause, 3) send KMS/CMK architecture by 12/16, 4) propose pilot scope and timeline by 12/19.
06:38 Marta: Sounds good. We'll prepare redacted PHI samples and set up a follow-up deep dive with Liam and Priya.
06:43 Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with artifacts and a calendar invite for the technical session.
06:50 End
